text: There is a reason why the laws of physics resist the freezing of time so violently.
In modern quantum mechanics, physical reality only manifests through continuous quantum interactions.
The universe is governed by the Second Law of Thermodynamics: the principle that entropy, or disorder, must always increase.
The relentless increase of entropy is what physicists call the Arrow of Time.
It is the reason why an egg can crack open and scramble, but a scrambled egg can never spontaneously reassemble itself into an intact shell.
Time is not a background clock ticking away on some cosmic wall.
Time is the measure of state transitions, molecular entanglements, and information flow.

To pause time is to demand that the entire quantum information matrix of the universe cease to change state, while expecting a single biological observer to process thoughts, form memories, and observe the surroundings.
But biological thought requires chemical metabolism, ion channels opening across brain cells, and ATP hydrolysis—all of which generate entropy.
You cannot exist outside the thermodynamic arrow without violating the conservation of energy itself.
